sentences.text: Stability is about where the weight is.
G is the center of gravity, which pulls down.
B is the center of buoyancy, the center of the underwater hull, which pushes up.
When the boat heels, B moves toward the low side, and the two forces create a righting arm, labeled G Z, that pushes the boat back upright.
M, the metacenter, is where the vertical line through B crosses the centerline.
The distance from G up to M is called the metacentric height, G M.
A bigger G M means more initial stability.
